title: MAGIC: Multi-User Advanced Graphic Immersive Configurator for Sustainable Customization of Complex Design Products – A Sailing Yacht Case Study
content: Modern design products are increasingly complex and hold greater emotional value, requiring versatile and collaborative customization. However, flexible multi-user, photorealistic Virtual Reality (VR) systems for product configuration remain limited, as shown by an analysis of literature and commercial solutions. To address these gaps, this paper introduces MAGIC (Multi-user Advanced Graphic Immersive Configurator). It provides a collaborative cross-platform environment with optimized graphics and ergonomic validation via digital avatars, overcoming the limitations of 2D visualization and existing tools. MAGIC can reduce CO2 emissions through prototype dematerialization and boost the global competitiveness of small and medium enterprises (SMEs), while its versatility enables future VR applications in other industries. MAGIC is applied to yacht design as a case study to evaluate its usability by conducting user testing, n=30. Participants collaborated in paired sessions to customize a high-performance sailing yacht and assess VR potential for configuring complex products. Results demonstrate MAGIC’s feasibility in a nautical scenario, reducing transportation costs and environmental impacts of client meetings and trade fairs. Additionally, it achieves a high usability score (SUS=80.83). Positive user feedback highlights that high-quality graphics and additional content significantly enhance immersion and engagement. However, encountered challenges with navigation methods and spatial perception indicate areas for improvement.
